versions.change: First published eligibility, selection, conflict, rail, independence, and reporting rules.

changePolicy: A change to eligibility, selection criteria, payment rails, independence rules, or reporting publishes a new version. It applies only to rounds announced at least 14 days after it is published. A round keeps the version it was announced under.

areas.name: Public repositories
eligibility: The repository is public, and anyone can read and clone it without an account.
The code or content is under an OSI-approved or Creative Commons license.
Where it is hosted does not matter: forkmesh.com, a self-hosted mirror, or another forge.

areas.name: Volunteer mirrors
eligibility: The applicant operates a public mirror, relay, or gateway that people other than the operator have used for at least 60 days.
The service publishes a health endpoint or status page.

areas.name: Accessibility
eligibility: The work improves a ForkMesh-compatible client, website, or document against WCAG 2.2 AA or the platform's accessibility guidelines.
The plan includes testing with at least one person who uses assistive technology.

areas.name: Documentation
eligibility: Public documentation, translations, or tutorials under an open license.

areas.name: Education
eligibility: Courses, workshops, or learning materials about decentralized collaboration, under an open license and free to attend or read.

areas.name: Ecosystem tooling
eligibility: An independent client, relay, index, verifier, or library with a public https source under an OSI-approved license.
A certification badge is welcome but not required.

generalEligibility: Individuals, informal groups, and organizations in any jurisdiction the funder can lawfully pay may apply.
Applying, being reviewed, and being paid need no ForkMesh account, plan, client, wallet, or token.
The operator of forkmesh.com and people it pays are not eligible for awards.
A round's funders and reviewers are not eligible in that round.
Work whose use requires a paid plan on any ForkMesh-operated service is not eligible.

offers.name: Donation
offers.description: A one-off gift to the public-interest pool. A donor may restrict a gift to an area, but never to a named recipient.
offers.eligibility: Anyone may donate. Gifts that carry conditions beyond an area restriction are declined.
offers.selection: Donations join the pool of the next announced round in their area.

offers.name: Recurring sponsorship
offers.description: Monthly or yearly support for the pool or one area. A sponsor can stop at any time.
offers.eligibility: Anyone may sponsor. Sponsorship buys no placement, ranking, seat, vote, or say in selection.
offers.selection: Sponsorship funds rounds in the sponsored area. Sponsors are listed as funders of the rounds they fund.

offers.name: Targeted grant
offers.description: A milestone-based award chosen in a published round for work in one area.
offers.eligibility: The area eligibility and general eligibility rules.
offers.selection: Disclosed reviewers score the published selection criteria. Awards go to eligible applications above the minimum score, in score order, within the pool and the concentration limits.

offers.name: Matching
offers.description: The pool matches public contributions a recipient raised on their own portable rail, up to a published ratio and cap.
offers.eligibility: The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. Matched contributions need public receipts.
offers.selection: Scored like a targeted grant. The award may not exceed the matched contributions times the ratio.

selectionCriteria.description: How many people outside the applicant benefit, and how directly.
Whether the milestones, budget, and schedule are realistic for the applicant.
Whether the work serves people with disabilities, low bandwidth, or languages the ecosystem under-serves.
Whether the result keeps working, or is handed on, after the award ends.
Whether the work adds a new operator, region, implementation, or maintainer, and so reduces concentration.

review.reviewerPool: Reviewers are participants with a current disclosure in conformance/governance/v1/participants.json. An independent reviewer is not a ForkMesh maintainer.

conflicts.recusal: A reviewer who is the applicant, or who shares an employer or funder with the applicant, must record a recusal and must not score that application. Any other conflict a reviewer declares is recorded and recused the same way.
conflicts.funders: A funder never reviews, never chooses a recipient, and may restrict a gift only to an area.

administrativeCost.statement: Administrative cost covers payment fees, accounting, and reviewer stipends. It is published per round before applications open.

paymentRails.name: Bank transfer (SEPA, ACH, or international wire)
Open Collective, through the recipient's own fiscal host
Solana transfer to an address the recipient controls
paymentRails.note: Optional. Never the only rail a round offers.

independence.statement: An award, donation, or sponsorship pays for work. It never changes who can reach a repository, what an identity may do, who votes, or what the network requires.

reporting.outcomeReport: Every reported or cancelled round publishes funds raised, awarded, and disbursed; administrative cost; recipients; milestone completion; operators funded and retained; accessibility impact; and lessons. A cancelled round publishes why.

communityReview.channels: Anyone may comment through an issue on any forge mirror of forkmesh/forkmesh or by email. A maintainer records each finding with attribution.

measures: funds raised, awarded, and disbursed per round
administrative cost as a share of the pool
volunteer-mirror operators funded and still operating at the outcome report
accessibility awards and reported accessibility impact
largest recipient, area, and funder share of a round

rounds.title: Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation
rounds.summary: Milestone grants and matching for people who run public mirrors, make ForkMesh-compatible clients and documents accessible, and write open documentation. Recipients choose their own payment rail.

applicationChannels.description: An issue labelled funding-application on any forge mirror of forkmesh/forkmesh.
Email to the address in the round announcement, for applicants who cannot apply in public.

opensWhen: A funder commits the pool and publishes the amount, source, conflicts, and any area restriction.
Administrative cost is published and stays within 10% of the pool.
At least three reviewers with current governance disclosures are seated, and at least one is not a ForkMesh maintainer.
The application window is announced with at least 21 days to apply.
rounds.note: No funder has committed a pool and no reviewer is seated, so the round has not opened. It has no applications, selections, or disbursements to report.
